scenes.narration: A synchronous motor turns at exactly the speed of the supply, no matter the load. Let's see why.
Three AC currents, each shifted by 120 degrees, feed the stator windings.
Together they create a magnetic field that rotates around the stator at synchronous speed.
That speed depends only on the supply frequency and the number of poles.
The DC-excited rotor locks onto this field and follows it. More load only increases the angle between them, not the speed.

params.text: A synchronous motor runs at exactly the speed of the rotating field.

scenes.narration: Constant speed regardless of load, as long as it stays in step.
